name: Afterlife Dreams
author: Diz_Chrome Dealer
description:
A R/R/B - a spin on the R/R/x shell with the efficient units in 6th Streets and Psycho Squads in the early game. Meredith provides a good blocker body and some recursion for the grind-y matches. Rogue and Nomad V provide value engines and help fund the combat tricks to help keep our board extra sticky. Then there is Yorinobu, 7 eddies for a minimum 12 power on board. Johnny and Wreckers round out the top end of threats.
Mantis blades, cheap but very impactful. Satori fill a similar role with the added bonus of card draw on won fights. Both provide enough power to help units like Johnny and Yorinobu hit the 10 power threshold or help Rogue survive a towerfall.
Might Experiment with Evelyn over Wakako, Wakako is either a draw 1 or a combat trick, while Evelyn would proc on 11 of the units allowing for a greater action economy.
Sideboard having 2 royce and 1 Meredith for the B/B/G Judy lists. 2 Detonate to mess with Gear heavy lists.

name: Paired Gig Theme Deck
author: Analog_V
description:
This deck is from a set of 4 theme decks focusing on the gig dice mechanics each color utilizes. I created these to help folks who have experience in other TCGs learn a bit more about why the values on gig dice matter, and to introduce each color’s mechanical identity in a format that hopefully is relatively balanced. This one focuses on Green's Paired Gigs mechanics.
For this deck, I didn't want to just copy the BBG Hanako lists as they overlaps too much with min gigs, but I also wanted to try and avoid using the same support cards across all decks in the series. So, I landed on GGG, with a very light Arasaka subtheme in Goro (Unit) and Sandayu Oda. I thought about using Pepe Najarro, but that pushed me towards V Corpo Exile, which is used in other decks in the series (since the blue gig-manipulation support cards are super flexible). I considered Rogue legend and Goro Bodyguard, but ultimately abandoned those as well in favor of the current split. Thank you for taking a look!

name: Min Gig Theme Deck
author: Analog_V
description:
This deck is from a set of 4 theme decks focusing on the gig dice mechanics each color utilizes. I created these to help folks who have experience in other TCGs learn a bit more about why the values on gig dice matter, and to introduce each color’s mechanical identity in a format that hopefully is relatively balanced. This one focuses on Blue's Min Gigs mechanics.
This deck was one of the smoother ones to put together, as I think there are a lot of powerful reasons to want min-gigs. Flathead, Three Mouths, and Pyramid Song are all well-tested cards that perform very well, so the building really came down to "How do I make this deck not just devolve into the meta BBG deck?" I settled on keeping some key interaction, but removing Maman and Towerfall, while also changing the legend to Padre to facilitate multiple min-gigs without the powerhouse of card draw that comes with Hanako. Thank you for taking a look!
